incident-bot: INCIDENT: [sev2] GPU node gpu-node-17 reporting repeated CUDA OOMs despite headroom. Autoscaler triggered, 120+ failed allocations in 2m. Paging inferred. PagerDuty alert -> oncall

rachel (oncall): on it. grabbing logs + isolating node. tagging eng-runtime.

marty (eng-runtime): thx. quick hypothesis: allocator slab fragmentation + reserved-block accounting mismatch. looks like headroom reported but blocks are unusable due to small-slab fragmentation. need nvml + runtime logs.

rachel (oncall): pasted nvml snapshot from the node:
```
NVIDIA-SMI 530.41.03    Driver Version: 530.41.03
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| GPU  Name        Persistence-M| Bus-Id        Disp.A | Volatile Uncorr. ECC |
| 17  A100-SXM4-80GB   On        | 00000000:3A:00.0 Off |                    0 |
| 0%   78C    P0   325W / 400W |  62132MiB / 81920MiB |
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
```

rachel (oncall): runtime log excerpt shows repeated failures: 
```
E runtime: allocate_chunk(size=24MB) -> CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY
E allocator: reserved_blocks_total=2048 reserved_blocks_free=132
E kvcache: active_reserve_blocks=1820 prefetch_queue=high
```

lena (eng-sre): that pattern screams "reserved blocks pinned by kv-cache + large prefetch + small-slab churn". mitigation options: 1) reduce kvcache reserve (soft) 2) trigger prefix cache eviction 3) soft-restart prefetch workers on that node. which do you want now?

rachel (oncall): doing (1) and (2) now. patching runtime env to lower REDWOOD_KVCACHE_RESERVE from 0.9 -> 0.6 on node pool. running rollout patch: 
```bash
kubectl -n inference patch deployment/redwood-runtime -p '{"spec":{"template":{"spec":{"containers":[{"name":"runtime","env":[{"name":"REDWOOD_KVCACHE_RESERVE","value":"0.6"}]}]}}}}'
```

ops-bot: Node gpu-node-17 cordoned by rachel. Draining pods (grace period 30s). Autoscaler will rehome critical workloads.

marty (eng-runtime): while that rollout happens, please trigger a soft-evict of KV cache on that node to free pinned blocks: 
```
curl -X POST "https://control-plane/_internal/evict-kv" -d '{"node":"gpu-node-17","mode":"soft"}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer <redacted>'
```

rachel (oncall): evict request sent, runtime acked. evicted ~1.8GB of kv pinned blocks according to the control response. monitoring OOM alerts.

alex (support): customer impact note: 2 tenants (acme-inc, healthco) saw request error spikes. 5xx rate rose from 0.1% baseline to 3.2% for ~4 minutes starting 3332109850. no data exfiltration. support tickets opened for both. informing CS.

ops-bot: Autoscaler pulled 3 pods off gpu-node-17, new pods scheduled on gpu-node-09/gpu-node-04. Node remains cordoned.

rachel (oncall): after evict + env patch, OOMs dropped to single-digit events/min. telemetry shows latency stable. keeping node cordoned for 10m then reprovision/replace.

jamie (eng-infra): long term: we should add a telemetry metric for "usable_reserved_blocks" (reserved_free - fragmentation_loss) and a fast-path to force compact small slabs when headroom exists but allocation fails. filing infra-ticket.

marty (eng-runtime): agree. also add a runtime guard: if CUDA OOM occurs and reserved_free>threshold, try incremental slab compaction + retry before surfacing OOM upstream.

rachel (oncall): creating incident channel #inc-3332109876 for postmortem. assigning pm: marty, postmortem owner: jamie, follow-ups: add usable_reserved_blocks metric, KV cache backpressure heuristics, node replacement playbook. monitoring window 15m.

marty (eng-runtime): thanks. ping me for timeline details. :thumbsup:

lena (eng-sre): noted. will add runbook step to cordon-and-evict when pv/kvcache pinned > 70%.

rachel (oncall): handing off to marty/jamie for postmortem and long-term mitigations. closing active responder loop. :white_check_mark:
